thread:
Maya: Customer asked for auditor-friendly evidence: deterministic audit events for critical actions, tamper-evident retention proofs, KMS key IDs for encrypted artifacts, and an export bundle format auditors can consume. They invoked SOC2, HIPAA, and 'FedRAMP-like' language.
sec-bot: note: secure-archival enabled for enterprise since 2024-10-01; default event_retention_days=90; sampling active on very high-volume endpoints.
Josh: quick recap of current state: we emit actor, action, resource, outcome routinely. We do not consistently include client_ip or kms_key_id in event bodies today. Also many hot-path endpoints are sampled (1/1000).
Priya: we do NOT log request/response bodies by default. For HIPAA/BAA customers we can provision encrypted payload capture to restricted buckets, but that needs legal sign-off and stricter RBAC.
Daniel: question for Maya: are they demanding full payloads or cryptographic proof of actions? Full payloads will trigger redaction rules and expand storage. Proofs can be lighter.
Maya: two asks from them: (1) verifiable events for critical ops (policy changes, KMS ops, exports), and (2) auditor validation: signed events, chain-of-custody, tamper evidence, plus retention proof. They also want an evidence delivery SLA.
Anna: engineering tradeoffs: storing full payloads increases PII risk and cost. Suggestion: emit a canonical event (who/what/when/outcome) plus payload_hash and a signature envelope signed by our KMS. Auditors can verify integrity without seeing contents.
Elena: contract perspective: customers will want retention term options (90/365/2555), export bundle format, signing method (our KMS vs customer HSM), delivery SLA (e.g., standard: 10 business days), and remedies if we fail to deliver. Legal will draft language but needs technical limits.
Josh: proposed audit schema v2 prototype (concept):
```
{
  "audit_schema_v": "2",
  "ts": "2025-06-12T15:23:45Z",
  "actor": "user:alice@example.com",
  "action": "role.assign",
  "resource": "org/123/role/dev",
  "outcome": "success",
  "meta": { "client_ip": "1.2.3.4", "region": "us-east-1" },
  "payload_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "signature": "kms:sign:v1:base64sig",
  "kms_key_id": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1234"
}
```
Maya: ok. We must ensure backward compatibility. Any schema additions should be behind a runtime flag and we should support v1 for a deprecation window.
Priya: operational constraints: add an 'always_log' override and map events tagged 'security_sensitive' to never be sampled. We also need to enumerate current sampled endpoints and exempt critical ops.
Daniel: implementation notes: SDKs and internal consumers must accept v2 while remaining compatible with v1. CI needs tests for signature verification and payload-hash checks.
Anna: UI/ops requirements: Dedicated/Private customers need toggles for: canonical-only, canonical+encrypted-payload, retention tier, and immutable-archive (S3 Object Lock / Glacier Vault Lock).
Elena: signing options: legal prefers customer-verifiable signatures. Options: sign with Redwood KMS and include signature + key id, or accept customer's public key/HSM for signing. Need threat model and feasibility input.
Maya: security items: redaction checklist, strict RBAC for export access, approval workflow for evidence downloads, and auditing of who accessed exported bundles. Update incident response playbook accordingly.
Josh: infra next steps: create schema PR (v2), feature flags for audit_v2 + always_log, storage design for retention tiers + immutable archives, and decide between per-event signing vs batched attestation.
Priya: ops next steps: inventory sampled endpoints, perf test signing (per-event latency), implement access logs for evidence buckets, and implement export throttles.
Daniel: dev tasks: SDK updates, event consumer changes, policy mapping for 'security_sensitive', and CI coverage.
Elena: legal tasks: draft evidence-delivery SLA addendum (propose 10 business days standard, expedited for fee), create contract clauses for retention tiers and signing options, coordinate with finance for cost numbers.
Sam (finance): need rough cost model: extra storage per retention tier, signing costs (per-event vs batch), retrieval/devops effort. Will produce a worksheet once we have estimated event volumes.
Maya: vuln triage note: payload logging expands blast radius. We'll run a threat model focusing on redaction rules, KMS ACLs, key rotation, and access approval flows. I'll pair with @Priya on the checklist.
Anna: owners and deadlines: Josh -> infra design + schema PR; Daniel -> SDKs + consumers; Priya -> sampling policy + perf; Maya -> threat model + rollout playbook; Elena -> contract and SLA draft; Sam -> cost estimates. Target: proposal + rough cost by EOD next Wed.
Maya: linking internal refs: https://redwood.internal/docs/audit-schema and https://redwood.internal/playbooks/audit-export
